description: Original SkillUP cube rotation set. Faces T/F/R use a right-handed cube frame. ▲ opposite ★, ● opposite ◆, ■ opposite +.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: Which option shows the same cube as the reference after rotation?
questions.imageAlt: A three-dimensional reference cube with a symbol on each top, front and right face, and four labelled 3D answer cubes A to D.
questions.tip: The circle moves to the top, square to the front and triangle to the right.
questions.explanation: A rotation can cycle three faces around a corner without reversing their order. In B, ● is on top, ■ at the front and ▲ on the right. The other options mirror the corner.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: Which cube can be obtained by rotating the reference cube?
questions.imageAlt: A three-dimensional reference cube with a symbol on each top, front and right face, and four labelled 3D answer cubes A to D.
questions.tip: Keep the clockwise order of the three faces, not only their symbols.
questions.explanation: The diamond, square and star cycle together: ◆ moves to the top, ■ to the front and ★ to the right. Only C keeps their original corner order.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: Which option is a real rotation, rather than a mirror image?
questions.imageAlt: A three-dimensional reference cube with a symbol on each top, front and right face, and four labelled 3D answer cubes A to D.
questions.tip: A physical rotation cannot reverse the handedness of the three corner faces.
questions.explanation: Option D, ▲ on top, ● at the front and ■ on the right, is a true rotation. The other three options reverse two faces and are mirror arrangements.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: Fold the net into a cube. Which option is impossible?
questions.imageAlt: A flat six-face cube net with original shapes, plus four possible answer cubes labelled A to D. Top, front and right faces of each cube are shown.
questions.tip: Check the opposite pairs before comparing the corners.
questions.explanation: The circle ● and diamond ◆ are opposite faces in the net, so they can never share an edge. A shows both as neighbours. B, C and D are possible rotations.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: The two diagrams show the same cube. Which symbol is opposite the star?
questions.imageAlt: Two views of the same six-symbol cube are shown as three-dimensional diagrams, with answer options A to D. The top, front and right faces are visible.
questions.tip: A face touches four neighbours, leaving one opposite face.
questions.explanation: The star ★ touches ●, +, ◆ and ■ across the two views. The only unaccounted symbol is ▲, so the triangle must be opposite the star.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: Fold the net into a cube. Which option correctly shows the star on top?
questions.imageAlt: A flat six-face cube net with original shapes, plus four possible answer cubes labelled A to D. Top, front and right faces of each cube are shown.
questions.tip: Place the star on top and check the order of the other two visible faces.
questions.explanation: With ★ on top and ◆ at the front, ■ is on the right in the genuine cube. C keeps the correct arrangement; the other options reverse the corner order.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: Which option shows the same cube after rotation?
questions.imageAlt: A three-dimensional reference cube with a symbol on each top, front and right face, and four labelled 3D answer cubes A to D.
questions.tip: Follow the diamond, plus and triangle around their shared corner.
questions.explanation: The ▲ / ◆ / + arrangement in B is a cyclic movement of the reference ◆ / + / ▲ corner. A, C and D reverse the orientation.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: Study the two views. Which cube cannot be formed?
questions.imageAlt: Two views of the same six-symbol cube are shown as three-dimensional diagrams, with answer options A to D. The top, front and right faces are visible.
questions.tip: First infer the opposite face pairs; then check three-face order.
questions.explanation: D reverses the triangle–square–circle corner. A, B and C are valid rotations consistent with both reference views. A cube cannot be reflected to make D.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: Two views keep the circle on top. Which symbol is opposite the triangle?
questions.imageAlt: Two views of the same six-symbol cube are shown as three-dimensional diagrams, with answer options A to D. The top, front and right faces are visible.
questions.tip: Keep the circle fixed and notice how the front and right faces change.
questions.explanation: The square moves from the front to the right while the circle stays on top. This reveals the quarter-turn, showing ★ on the opposite side from ▲. Answer B.

questions.name: Cube & Dice Rotation
questions.text: Using the cube net and reference view, which option is a valid rotation?
questions.imageAlt: A flat six-face cube net with original shapes, plus four possible answer cubes labelled A to D. Top, front and right faces of each cube are shown.
questions.tip: Check opposite pairs first, then the orientation of the three visible faces.
questions.explanation: C has ● on top, ■ at the front and ▲ on the right, which is a valid rotation. B puts opposite + and ■ together; A and D reverse the face order.
